# 7. Conclusion

Standardized effect sizes are the currency of cumulative science in
the behavioral disciplines, yet the routine neglect of measurement
error means that this currency is systematically debased. The
`measuredES` package provides a practical, theoretically grounded
toolkit for recovering effect sizes at the construct level for
independent-groups designs and meta-analytic synthesis.

The simulation results reported here demonstrate that the Spearman
correction performs as theory predicts, eliminating bias with
negligible RMSE cost at moderate to large sample sizes, and that
the Bonett confidence interval provides near-nominal coverage across
a wide range of conditions. The meta-analytic findings carry
particular weight: under the realistic scenario of heterogeneous
reliability across studies, uncorrected meta-analysis can fail to
contain the true effect in more than 70% of replications. Correcting
for measurement error is a prerequisite for valid cumulative
inference, not an esoteric refinement.

`measuredES` is freely available on GitHub
(https://github.com/gulince/measuredES) and is being prepared for
submission to the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN). All
simulation code and data are included in the package repository to
support full reproducibility.
